text:
vivian: Quick sync — product wants a concise battlecard and three email subject lines for the launch of our inference offering. Primary competitive targets: cloud-managed endpoints, vanilla LLM APIs, and DIY infra. Need drafts by EOD so design can mock slides.

omar: Agree. Let's center on outcomes: predictable tail latency, deterministic unit economics, and operational guardrails (canaries, fallback). Avoid raw price comparisons.

trina: Webinar hooks I like: 1) 'Inference you can SLAs on' (ops demo), 2) 'Stop billing surprises' (econ math), 3) 'Keep features live when models fail' (demo fallback). Each should have a 90s demo.

ash: For the battlecard, short top lines: 
- Headline: "Production-first inference: predictable performance, predictable spend"
- Why it matters: "Customers avoid outage surprises and runaway costs without rebuilding infra."

miles: Bench snippet (internal demo, 95th pct, 3k tokens) for slide note only:
- Redwood Dedicated: ~130ms
- Cloud-managed endpoint (anonymized): ~250ms
- LLM API provider: ~360ms
- DIY multi-tenant infra: ~420ms
footnote: methodology: demo workload, single-sequence profile; results vary by model and quantization.

legal-bot: Reminder: anonymize competitor labels (CloudZ / API-Q / DIY), no absolute cost claims, and include methodology blurb on the slide.

ovian: (ops-bot) webinar room check: Tue next week 9am PT available. Zoom Pro reserved.

vivian: Sales enablement asks: 1) three one-liners to use in SDR scripts, 2) three short objection handlers, 3) two landing copy variants.

omar: SDR one-liners: 
- Cloud-managed: "Fast to pilot. Redwood keeps features live and budgets stable at scale."
- LLM APIs: "Great prototypes. Redwood adds rollout controls and caching so production is safe."
- DIY infra: "Own your infra without the ops tax — Private gives control with a managed control plane."

trina: Objection handlers (short): 
- 'We already use cloud endpoints' -> 'Those are great for pilots. We reduce tail latency surprises and give fallbacks so your user-facing flows don't drop.'
- 'LLM APIs are cheaper' -> 'Prototype costs differ from sustained production costs — our estimator maps your token profile to projected spend.'
- 'We self-host to save money' -> 'Self-hosting shifts cost to engineering time. Private balances control with lower ongoing ops overhead.'

ash: Landing copy variants: 
Variant A (Engineer): "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and unit economics. One API, unified runtime, and rollout controls."
Variant B (Product Lead): "Deliver reliable AI experiences. Automatic fallbacks and verified latency profiles protect users when models misbehave."

miles: Email subject lines for A/B test: 
1) "Benchmarked: lower production tail latency for inference"
2) "How teams make inference costs predictable"
3) "Keep your AI features live when models fail"

ovian: Inbound routing recommendation: create tag 'launch-inference-signal' -> immediate send: one-pager + bench highlights; 48h follow-up: 90s demo clip; if sample tokens > threshold or regulated industry flag -> SDR touch and Private brief.

vivian: Good. Design note: slides should use anonymized competitor bars and a clear methodology footnote. No competitor logos. Also add a tiny flow diagram showing 'request -> routing -> cache -> model pools -> fallback'.

omar: Also include an internal Q/A cheat sheet: common customer questions and short answers (3 bullets each). I'll draft after lunch.

trina: Timeline: 
- by 3pm today: ash battlecard draft + objection handlers; miles bench artifact + slide copy; omar Q/A cheat sheet draft
- by EOD: two landing copy variants and the three email subjects consolidated
- ops-bot: confirm webinar slot and speakers by EOD.

ovian: ops-bot: webinar slot confirmed Tue next week 9:00 PT; speakers TBD. Calendar invite sent.

legal-bot: I'll review copy tomorrow morning for any risky claims.

vivian: One final editorial: avoid leading with 'we're cheaper'. Prefer 'predictable unit economics' or 'lower ops risk'. Great work — ping when drafts are in /marketing/webinar/prelaunch/. :rocket:
